rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis uses compression testing on as-solidified polycrystalline samples, while the target uses uniaxial tensile loading on a single crystal via molecular dynamics simulation. These are fundamentally different kinds of studies (experimental vs. simulation, compression vs. tension, polycrystal vs. single crystal).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies quasi-static to high strain rates (10⁻⁴–2100 s⁻¹) and room/elevated temperatures, while the target uses extremely high strain rates (10⁸–10¹⁰ s⁻¹) and cryogenic to moderate temperatures (10–600 K) in a vacuum simulation. The regimes are completely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis proposes dislocation accumulation and adiabatic shear band formation as the key mechanism, whereas the target describes yielding via dislocation nucleation at vacancy sites, mediated by Shockley partials and stacking faults, with no shear bands. These are contradictory mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts increased yield strength and strain-rate sensitivity at high strain rates and low temperatures, while the target finds yield strength is insensitive to strain rate and decreases with temperature. The predicted outcomes are opposite in direction regarding strain-rate sensitivity.
